mainTopic: How a husband's vow against his wife works, why the limit is thirty days, and why a פרנס who supports her is not his שליח.
overview: The משנה says that if a husband makes a נדר forbidding his wife to benefit from him, he must appoint a פרנס for up to thirty days, and after that he must divorce her. The גמרא first asks how his vow can work at all if he owes her food. It settles on the case where he told her to live off her own earnings. Those earnings cover her basic needs, and the פרנס supplies small extras she had in her father's house and now demands because of the vow. The thirty-day limit exists because after that people hear about it and it shames her. A second answer says he vowed while she was an ארוסה whose wedding date had passed. A third answer, that she married him after the vow, is rejected. Then the גמרא asks how a פרנס is not simply the husband's שליח. רב הונא answers that the husband only announces 'whoever feeds her will not lose out,' and the גמרא defends this from a case in גיטין, from רבי אמי's fire rule, and from רבה's challenge from a משנה in נדרים. Finally it quotes that משנה in full, including the ways to help someone who may not benefit from you, and רבי יוסי's dissent, whose reason רבא begins to explain on the next amud.

steps.title: We treat it as if he told her to support herself
steps.stepSummary: The end of the first answer: the husband is treated as if he told his wife to use her earnings for her food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is considered as if he said to her: 'Take your earnings in place of your food.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer the גמרא started just before. It explains how the husband's vow can work even though he owes his wife food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband may tell his wife: 'Keep your earnings and feed yourself.' Since he has that power, we treat his vow as if he had used it. So he no longer owes her food, and his vow does not cancel any debt he owes her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is treated as if he said
Take your earnings in place of your food
A wife's earnings from her work
Food and support the husband owes his wife

phrases.english: he is considered as one who says to her:
'Take your earnings in place of your food.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question (from before this section) of how the husband's vow can work if he owes her food.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal fiction: an option he could use is treated as already used.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His vow cannot work, because he already owes her food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he could swap her earnings for her food, we treat him as having done so, so the vow works.

steps.title: A challenge from רב הונא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: If 'he could say it' counts as 'he said it', then the same should apply to the wife in רב הונא's case. But it doesn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ruling of רב הונא in the name of רב is correct (a wife may say 'I won't take your food and I won't work for you'), then why does a husband not need to cancel his wife's vow 'Whatever I make for you is forbidden like a קרבן'? Using the same logic, we should say: since she could say 'I won't take food and won't work,' it is as if she said it, and then her vow should really work, so he would need to cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first answer. It shows that the idea 'if you could say it, it's as if you said it' leads to a wrong result in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says a wife may give up her food so she can keep her earnings. If 'could say' equals 'did say', then her vow on her work should count as if she had already given up her food, so her work is hers and the vow takes hold. But the known ruling is that the husband does not need to cancel this vow, so we don't treat her as if she said it. So why treat the husband that way?

keyTerms.meaning: And if that ruling is correct
I won't take your food, and I won't work for you
A word for making a vow that forbids something like a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who is talking. In the משנה the HUSBAND makes the vow. In רב הונא's case the WIFE makes the vow. The גמרא uses the wife's case to test the logic of the husband's case.

phrases.english: But if that ruling is correct,
the one Rav Huna said in the name of Rav,
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
a woman may say to her husband:
'I will not be fed by you and I will not work for you,'
then when she says 'What I make for your mouth is forbidden like a konam,'
why does he not need to cancel it?
Let us say: since she is able to say,
'I will not be fed and I will not work,'
she is considered as one who says to him:
'I will not be fed and I will not work.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'he could say it' counts as 'he said it.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that idea were true, it would apply to the wife in רב הונא's case too, and then her vow would take effect and he would need to cancel it. But the ruling is that he doesn't need to cancel it, so the idea must be wrong.

steps.title: Retraction: he actually told her to support herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops 'it is as if he said' and explains the משנה as a case where he really said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, don't say 'it is considered as if.' Instead, the משנה is talking about a case where he actually says to her: 'Take your earnings in place of your food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back its first answer. Now the משנה is about a husband who really told his wife to use her earnings for her food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'could say' is no longer treated as 'did say', the vow only works if he actually made the swap. Once he really said it, he no longer owes her food, so his vow cancels no debt.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the גמרא is changing its answer)

phrases.english: Rather, do not say 'he is considered as if,'
but rather, it is where he actually says to her:
'Take your earnings in place of your food.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by giving up the idea of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow works because he could have swapped her earnings for her food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow works only because he actually made that swap.

steps.title: Then why does she need a trustee?
steps.stepSummary: If she supports herself from her earnings, why does the משנה require a פרנס?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does she need a פרנס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If she is supporting herself, the משנה's rule about appointing a פרנס seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרנס is a go-between who gives her what the husband owes. But if he has already stopped owing her food, there is nothing left for a פרנס to deliver.

keyTerms.meaning: A trustee or go-between who gives the wife her support

phrases.english: If so, why does she need a trustee?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of a פרנס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she lives off her own earnings, the husband owes her nothing, so a פרנס has nothing to give her.

steps.title: Her earnings are not enough
steps.stepSummary: The case is where her earnings don't cover all her needs, so the פרנס gives the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where her earnings are not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that her earnings don't cover everything, so the פרנס is needed to give her the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the swap, the husband still owes whatever her earnings don't cover. The פרנס provides that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it is not enough for her

phrases.english: It is where her earnings are not enough for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her earnings cover everything, so no פרנס is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her earnings fall short, so a פרנס covers the rest.

steps.title: The original problem comes back
steps.stepSummary: If her earnings fall short, he still owes her the rest, so how can his vow work?
steps.simpleTranslation: If her earnings are not enough, then our question returns to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer of step 5 brings back the original question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he still owes her part of her food, his vow forbids her from something he is obligated to give. That is exactly the first problem: how can his vow cancel what he owes her?

keyTerms.meaning: Our question returns to its place

phrases.english: If it is where her earnings are not enough,
then our question returns to its place!
phrases.notes: The question from before this section: how can he forbid her from what he already owes her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5 by showing it brings back the original problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that her earnings are not enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he still owes her something, his vow again cancels a debt he owes her, and that should not be possible.

steps.title: רב אשי: enough for big things, not small things
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says her earnings cover her main needs but not small extras.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is where her earnings are enough for the big things but not enough for the small things.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a middle case. Her earnings cover her basic needs, and only small extras are missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her basic food is covered by her own earnings, so the vow does not take away her core support. The small extras that are missing are what the פרנס provides.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is where her earnings are enough for big things,
but are not enough for small things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי בְּמַסְפֶּקֶת לִדְבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting her needs into basic needs and extras
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either her earnings cover all her needs or they leave a real debt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her basic needs are covered and only small extras are missing. The פרנס provides those.

steps.title: What are these small things?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which small things are meant. Either way there seems to be a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: These small things, what is the case? If she is used to them, then she is used to them, and he owes them to her like anything else. And if she is not used to them, why does she need a פרנס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer by asking what kind of small things these are. Both possibilities seem to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is used to these things, they count as real needs he must provide, and the original problem returns. If she is not used to them, he doesn't owe them, so there is nothing for a פרנס to give.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: These small things, what is the case?
If she is used to them,
then she is used to them!
phrases.notes: Meaning: then they count as real needs he owes her, and the old problem is back.

phrases.english: And if she is not used to them,
why does she need a trustee?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is used to them, he owes them and the vow problem returns. If she isn't, he doesn't owe them and no פרנס is needed.

steps.title: Things she had at home and gave up for him
steps.stepSummary: The small things are ones she had in her father's home and went without in the marriage. Now that he has made the vow, she demands them again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed where she was used to them in her father's house, but she put up with living without them with him. She says to him: 'Until now, when you had not made a vow against us, I put up with it for your sake. Now that you have made a vow against us, I can't put up with it for your sake anymore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a case in between the two options of step 8. She was used to these things but chose to give them up while married to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she gave them up willingly, he was not actually paying for them, so his vow does not cancel something he was paying her. But after his vow hurt her, she may take back her favor and demand them, and the פרנס provides them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this case)
She puts up with it for his sake
You made a vow against us

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case: the husband told his wife to live off her earnings. Those earnings cover her basic needs. The פרנס gives her the small extras she had at home and gave up for him, which she now demands because of his vow.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where she was used to them in her father's house,
and she was putting up with going without them, for his sake,
for she says to him:
'Until now, when you had not made a vow against us,
I put up with it for your sake;
now that you have made a vow against us,
I cannot put up with it for your sake anymore.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 with a third, in-between case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a middle case between the two options
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Small things are either owed in full or not owed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: These are things she was used to but gave up for him. He was not paying for them, yet after his vow she may demand them through a פרנס.

steps.title: Why is thirty days the limit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes thirty days special in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about up to thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows the case (small extras she wants from him again). It asks why the משנה draws the line at thirty days. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is settled: she gets small extras through a פרנס. So why must he divorce her after thirty days? Something must change at that point, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: A go-between who supports her for the husband

phrases.english: And what is different about up to thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case defined in step 9 and asks about the משנה's time limit
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the משנה's cutoff is exactly thirty days

steps.title: Before thirty days people don't hear about it
steps.stepSummary: For a short time people don't notice and she is not shamed. After that people hear, and it becomes shameful for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to thirty days people don't hear about her, and the matter is not demeaning for her. Longer than that, people hear about her, and it is demeaning for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that thirty days is the point where people start noticing. Once they notice, it shames her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting her extras through a go-between instead of from her husband is embarrassing if people find out. For thirty days it stays quiet. After that it becomes known and shames her, so he must divorce her and pay the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is demeaning for her

phrases.aramaic: עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם לֹא שָׁמְעִי בַּהּ אִינָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Up to thirty days, people do not hear about her
phrases.notes: "Hear about her" means people don't find out that she gets her needs through a go-between.

phrases.english: and the matter is not demeaning for her;
longer than that, people hear about her
and the matter is demeaning for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם לֹא שָׁמְעִי בַּהּ אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After thirty days the arrangement becomes public and shameful for her
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: the vow works because her earnings cover her main needs and the פרנס gives only small extras. After thirty days it becomes public and shameful, so he must divorce her.

steps.title: Another answer: he made the vow while she was only betrothed
steps.stepSummary: A new way to explain how the vow works: he made it while she was an ארוסה, before he owed her food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say that he made the vow when she was a betrothed woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier problem: how can his vow work if he must feed her? It offers a new answer. He made the vow while she was only an ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a vow cannot cancel a duty he already has. If he vowed before he owed her food, the vow takes hold. This answer does not need the earnings and small-extras explanation at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (an alternative answer)
He made a vow against her
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before נישואין

phrases.english: If you wish, say
that he made the vow against her when she was a betrothed woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the kind of problem raised in step 6, instead of the רב אשי line
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (timing of the vow)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow could not work, since he already owed her food
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow was made before he owed her food, so it takes hold

steps.title: Does a betrothed woman even get food?
steps.stepSummary: If she is only betrothed, she gets no food from him anyway, so why would a פרנס be needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a betrothed woman have food from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. An ארוסה normally gets no food from her husband, so the vow should change nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires a פרנס to support her, so she must have a right to food. But an ארוסה usually has none. So the case does not seem to fit the משנה.

phrases.english: Does a betrothed woman have food from him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the case is about an ארוסה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ארוסה has no right to food, so the משנה's arrangement with a פרנס would make no sense

steps.title: The wedding date arrived but they did not marry
steps.stepSummary: The case is an ארוסה whose wedding date came and went, and in that case she does get food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where the time arrived and they did not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is a special ארוסה. Her set wedding date has passed without a wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wedding date passes, the husband starts owing her food even before the wedding. He vowed while she was an ארוסה, and later the food duty began. So she needs a פרנס.

phrases.english: Where the time arrived and they did not marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A betrothed woman never gets food
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the wedding date passes, an ארוסה does get food

steps.title: Proof from a משנה that she eats from his food
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that once the wedding date passes, such women eat from the husband's food and from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if the time arrived and they did not marry, they eat from his food and eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a משנה. It shows that an ארוסה whose wedding date passed eats from the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה shows the husband owes her food at this stage. So a vow made earlier, while she was an ארוסה, can block it, and a פרנס is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: if the time arrived and they did not marry,
phrases.notes: This משנה is earlier in this מסכת, on 57a.

phrases.english: they eat from his food, and they eat תרומה.
phrases.notes: The תרומה part applies when the husband is a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 14 with a source
steps.raayaObject: That an ארוסה whose wedding date passed gets food from the husband

steps.title: In this case, why thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: If she is still an ארוסה, the shame reason may not fit, so why thirty days?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about up to thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again why the limit is thirty days, now inside the new ארוסה answer. It is getting ready to give a new reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was shame. People would see a wife getting her needs through a go-between. In this new answer the גמרא wants a reason that fits a woman who is still an ארוסה.

phrases.english: And what is different about up to thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the משנה's time limit fits the ארוסה answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A reason for the thirty-day cutoff that fits the ארוסה case
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as step 10 asked again for no reason. The גמרא repeats it because the case has changed, and it needs a new answer.

steps.title: After thirty days the go-between stops doing his job well
steps.stepSummary: For thirty days the פרנס does his job properly. After that he starts to neglect her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to thirty days the agent does his job. Longer than that, the agent does not do his job.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a go-between can be trusted to look after her well for about thirty days, but not longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason here is not shame. It is that the system stops working. Over time the פרנס gets lazy and she suffers, so after thirty days he must divorce her and pay the כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם עָבֵיד שָׁלִיחַ שְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Up to thirty days, the agent carries out his task;
phrases.notes: The "agent" is the פרנס who supports her in the husband's place.

phrases.english: longer than that, the agent does not carry out his task.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם עָבֵיד שָׁלִיחַ שְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After thirty days the פרנס will neglect her, so the arrangement can no longer continue
steps.whatToRemember: Second approach: he vowed while she was an ארוסה whose wedding date had passed. The thirty-day limit is about the go-between losing his care for her over time.

steps.title: A third answer: he vowed while she was betrothed, and then she married him
steps.stepSummary: The vow was made while she was an ארוסה, and afterward she married him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say that he made the vow when she was betrothed, and then she married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to explain how the vow can work. It was made while she was an ארוסה, and only later did she marry him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here she is fully married, so he clearly owes her food. But the vow came first, before that duty began, so it takes hold. The case does not need the passed-wedding-date idea.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
that he made the vow against her when she was betrothed, and then she married.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא שֶׁהִדִּירָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא אֲרוּסָה וְנִישֵּׂאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to the problem of how the vow works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vow cannot cancel food he already owes
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow came before the marriage, so it takes hold

steps.title: She married him knowing about the vow
steps.stepSummary: If she married him after the vow, she knew and agreed to it. So why should he have to divorce her?
steps.simpleTranslation: She married. She knew about it and accepted it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the third answer. By marrying him after the vow, she agreed to live with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forces him to divorce her and pay the כתובה after thirty days. But if she knowingly accepted the vow, she seems to have no complaint. So why should he be forced?

keyTerms.meaning: She considered it and accepted it

phrases.english: She married? Then she understood it and accepted it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that she married after the vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying with full knowledge means she accepted the vow, so the משנה should not force a divorce for her sake

steps.title: She thought she could handle it, but now she can't
steps.stepSummary: She says she thought she could accept it, but now she sees she cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where she says: I thought I could accept it, but now I cannot accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that she married thinking she could live with the vow. Now she finds she cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her agreement was based on a wrong guess about how hard it would be. Living with it showed her it was too much. So her earlier agreement does not stop her, and the משנה's ruling applies.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרָה: כִּסְבוּרָה אֲנִי שֶׁאֲנִי יְכוֹלָה לְקַבֵּל,
phrases.english: Where she says: I thought that I could accept it;
now I am not able to accept it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרָה כִּסְבוּרָה אֲנִי שֶׁאֲנִי יְכוֹלָה לְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marrying after the vow means she gave up any complaint
steps.terutzMaskana: She can say she thought she could bear it and now finds she cannot
steps.whatToRemember: Third approach: he vowed while she was an ארוסה, then they married, and she says she thought she could bear it but now cannot. The next step rejects this approach.

steps.title: Blemishes are different from food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer that she can say 'I thought I could accept it.' That reasoning works for מומין, but not for מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say we use that reasoning for blemishes. But do we use it for food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 20. It says that answer only works for blemishes, not for food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מומין, a wife can later say 'I thought I could live with it, but I can't,' and that is accepted. A lack of food is not like that. If she agreed to it when she married, she cannot later back out with that excuse. So the answer from step 20 does not fit our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say (we grant this much)

phrases.english: You can say that we say this regarding blemishes;
phrases.notes: For blemishes, a woman can say 'I thought I could handle it, but I can't.'

phrases.english: but regarding food, do we say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The answer in step 20 that she can say she thought she could accept it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reasoning applies to מומין, not to lack of מזונות

steps.title: Back to the original answers
steps.stepSummary: Since the last answer failed, the גמרא concludes that the earlier answers are the correct ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the answer is as we explained at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the newer answer and goes back to the explanations it gave earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of 'she married him after the vow' could not be defended. So the גמרא returns to its first explanations of the משנה, which do not have this problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear (the clear answer is)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'she agreed when she married' approach is dropped. The גמרא keeps its original explanations of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at first.
phrases.notes: He means the earlier answers, like the case where he vowed while she was an ארוסה and they were not yet married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the rejection in step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is explained by the earlier answers, not by the idea that she married him knowing about the vow.

steps.title: Isn't the provider just the husband's agent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about a פרנס and asks how it works. If the פרנס is the husband's שליח, the wife is still getting benefit from the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that for up to thirty days, he appoints a provider. But isn't the provider acting as his agent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about the פרנס and asks a strong question on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband made a נדר that forbids his wife to get any benefit from him. A שליח counts like the person who sent him. So if the פרנס is his שליח, she is still getting benefit from the husband, and the נדר is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: A provider or manager who supplies her needs

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether a פרנס is allowed to help her. It is about whether the help still counts as coming from the husband, which the נדר forbids.

phrases.english: Up to thirty days, he appoints a provider.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: But isn't the provider acting as his agent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that he appoints a פרנס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שליח counts like the sender, so she would still be getting benefit from the husband

steps.title: He only says: whoever feeds her will not lose out
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the husband does not appoint a real agent. He just announces that anyone who feeds her will not lose out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The case is where he says, 'Whoever feeds her will not lose out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by explaining what the משנה means by 'appointing a פרנס.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband does not send anyone. Whoever feeds her does it by his own choice, and later the husband pays him back. So the food does not come from the husband through a שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: Will not lose out (will be paid back)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between sending a שליח and just promising to pay back whoever chooses to help.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is where he says: "Whoever feeds her will not lose out."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, בְּאוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַזָּן אֵינוֹ מַפְסִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרנס is a real שליח of the husband
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband only promises payment to whoever chooses to feed her, so there is no שליחות

steps.title: The man in the pit: a general announcement can create agents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a משנה in גיטין. There, a general call to 'whoever hears' makes the listeners into agents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when he says this, isn't the person acting as his agent? We learned: A man thrown into a pit said, 'Whoever hears my voice should write a גט for my wife.' Those people should write it and give it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's answer. It uses a case where a general announcement to anyone does create agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pit case, the man spoke to no one in particular. Still, whoever heard him became his שליח, because a get must be written by the husband's agent. So a general statement like 'whoever feeds' should also make the feeder his שליח.

phrases.english: And when he says this,
isn't the person acting as his agent?
But we learned:
One who was thrown into a pit,
and said: "Whoever hears his voice
should write a bill of divorce for his wife"
these people should write it and give it!
phrases.notes: They can only do this as his agents, so his general call made them agents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמַר הָכִי לָאו שְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ קָעָבֵיד? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that 'whoever feeds' creates no שליחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the pit case, a general call to anyone still makes the listeners into agents

steps.title: A command versus a promise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. In the pit case he gave a command, 'should write.' Here he only said 'whoever feeds,' which is a promise and not a command.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There he says 'should write.' Here, does he say 'should feed'? He says 'whoever feeds'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by showing that the two cases are worded differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Should write' tells people to act, so they become his שליחים. 'Whoever feeds will not lose out' gives no order. It only promises to pay back anyone who chooses to help. So no שליחות is created, and רב הונא's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (these are not alike)

steps.whatToRemember: A command ('should write') creates שליחות. A promise to pay back helpers ('whoever feeds will not lose out') does not. So the פרנס is not the husband's שליח, and the wife does not get benefit from him.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There he says "should write,"
but here, does he say "should feed"?
He says "whoever feeds"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 and defends רב הונא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by their wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any general announcement creates שליחות, like in the pit case
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a command creates שליחות. 'Whoever feeds' is a promise, not a command.

steps.title: Challenge from the fire rule of רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. רבי אמי allowed the line 'whoever puts out the fire will not lose out' only in a fire. That seems to mean that in other cases this line is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אמי said: in a fire on שבת, the חכמים allowed a person to say, 'Whoever puts it out will not lose out.' The words 'in a fire' come to leave out what? Don't they leave out a case like ours?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's answer from step 24 by pointing out that רבי אמי allowed the 'will not lose out' line only for a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'whoever ___ will not lose out' were never a way of appointing a שליח, there would be no need for a special allowance limited to a fire. So the limit 'in a fire' suggests that in normal cases, like the wife's פרנס, this line is not allowed. That would undo רב הונא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who puts out (the fire)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ami say:
In the case of a fire, they permitted saying:
phrases.notes: This is a fire on שבת. He says it near non-Jews, who may then put the fire out.

phrases.english: "Whoever puts it out will not lose out."
"In the case of a fire" comes to exclude what?
Isn't it to exclude a case like this one?!
phrases.notes: 'A case like this' means our case, where a husband feeds his wife through someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 26 defended רב הונא from the גיטין משנה, the גמרא brings a new challenge against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that 'whoever feeds her will not lose out' does not make anyone an agent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי limits the allowance to a fire. That implies the same phrase is not allowed elsewhere, which means it does work like appointing an agent.

steps.title: The fire rule only excludes other שבת prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'in a fire' does not exclude cases like ours. It only means this kind of hint was allowed for a fire, and not for other kinds of שבת work.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'In a fire' comes to exclude the other prohibitions of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge by explaining what the words 'in a fire' really leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit to a fire is about שבת laws. Even hinting to a non-Jew to do מלאכה is a problem, and the חכמים relaxed it only for a fire. It says nothing about whether 'will not lose out' makes someone a שליח, so רב הונא stands.

phrases.english: No, it is to exclude other prohibitions of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading what a limiting word excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In a fire' seemed to exclude any other case where someone says 'will not lose out', like the husband feeding his wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In a fire' only excludes other שבת prohibitions. It has nothing to do with appointing a שליח.

steps.title: רבה challenges from the storekeeper משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a משנה from מסכת נדרים. When a man may not benefit from his friend, the friend may only hint to a storekeeper that he does not know what to do for him. From this, רבה infers that saying openly 'whoever feeds him will not lose out' is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: if a person is forbidden by a נדר to benefit from his friend, and he has nothing to eat, the friend may go to a storekeeper he is used to dealing with. He says to him, 'So-and-so may not benefit from me, and I don't know what to do for him.' The storekeeper feeds him and later collects payment from the friend. Only this kind of hint is allowed. Saying 'whoever feeds him will not lose out' is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a משנה (from מסכת נדרים) that seems to show that only a vague hint is allowed. That would mean the open line 'whoever feeds will not lose out' is forbidden, against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the friend say only 'I don't know what to do for him.' רבה reads this to mean that anything stronger, like 'whoever feeds him will not lose out', would make the storekeeper his שליח. Then the food would count as benefit from the friend. If so, the husband's announcement about the פרנס would also be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: someone forbidden by a נדר from getting benefit

steps.confusionAlert: The person who goes to the storekeeper is not the one who is hungry. It is the friend whom he may not benefit from, who wants to help him.

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
One who is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend,
and he has nothing to eat —
he may go to a storekeeper whom he regularly deals with,
phrases.notes: The 'he' who goes is the friend who wants to help.

phrases.english: and say to him:
"So-and-so is forbidden by a vow to benefit from me,
and I don't know what I can do for him."
The storekeeper gives him food,
and comes and takes payment from this one.
This is what is permitted,
but "whoever feeds him will not lose out" — no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fire challenge was answered, רבה brings a second challenge against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that 'whoever feeds will not lose out' is allowed and does not create a שליח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows only a vague hint. That implies the clearer line 'whoever feeds will not lose out' is forbidden because it makes the listener an agent.

steps.title: The משנה teaches the harder case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching 'it goes without saying.' A general 'whoever feeds will not lose out', said to everyone, is surely allowed. The משנה teaches that even speaking to one familiar storekeeper is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that 'whoever feeds him will not lose out' is allowed, since that is said to the whole world. But here, since he is familiar with the storekeeper and goes to say it to him directly, you might think it is like telling him, 'Go, you give him food.' So the משנה teaches us that even this is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבה's reading around. The משנה's case is the stricter one, not the only one allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speaking to one specific, familiar person looks much more like giving an order to a שליח than a general announcement does. The משנה tells us that even this harder case is allowed. So a general announcement, like the husband's 'whoever feeds her', is certainly allowed, and רב הונא is supported.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it goes without saying'; the case taught is the bigger chiddush
to the whole world, in general

steps.whatToRemember: A general announcement such as 'whoever ___ will not lose out' does not make anyone a שליח. Even approaching one familiar storekeeper with a hint is allowed, as long as there is no direct command.

phrases.english: It is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
There is no need to say that "whoever feeds him will not lose out" is allowed —
since he is saying it to the whole world,
but this case,
since he is familiar with him
and goes and says it to him directly,
you might think it is like one who said to him: Go,
"you give it to him" —
so it teaches us that it is still allowed.
phrases.notes: Even though he went to a specific person, he gave no command, so the storekeeper is not his agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the case taught is the bigger חידוש, not the only permitted case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a hint to a storekeeper is allowed, and a general 'whoever feeds will not lose out' is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general announcement is surely allowed. The משנה adds that even a hint to one familiar person is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה itself: the storekeeper case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes the full משנה that רבה brought. It starts with the storekeeper case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the משנה itself: if a person is forbidden by a נדר to benefit from his friend and has nothing to eat, the friend goes to a storekeeper he regularly deals with. He says, 'So-and-so may not benefit from me, and I don't know what to do for him.' The storekeeper feeds him and later collects from the friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going back to quote the full משנה it just mentioned. This sets up the extra case that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'גופא' tell us the גמרא is leaving the argument and studying the source on its own. This first part repeats the storekeeper case word for word, as the opening of the full משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself'; returning to quote a source in full

phrases.english: The matter itself:
One who is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend
and has nothing to eat,
the friend goes to a storekeeper whom he regularly deals with,
and says to him:
"So-and-so is forbidden by a vow to benefit from me,
and I don't know what I can do for him."
The storekeeper gives him food,
and comes and takes payment from this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to quote in full the משנה that רבה cited in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A friend may indirectly arrange food for someone who may not benefit from him by hinting to a familiar storekeeper, who later collects from the friend.

steps.title: The same rule for hired workers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a parallel case. If the person needs building, fencing or reaping, the friend may hint to familiar workers in the same way, and they collect their wages from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he needs his house built, his fence put up, or his field reaped, the friend goes to workers he regularly hires. He tells them, 'So-and-so may not benefit from me, and I don't know what to do for him.' They work for him and later collect their wages from the friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and applies the same hinting method to hired workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not only about food. Any help, like labor, can be arranged with the same indirect hint. Since there is still no direct command, the workers are not the friend's שליחים, and the person is not getting forbidden benefit from him.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows a friend to help a מודר הנאה indirectly, with food or with work, by hinting to people he regularly deals with, without giving a direct order.

phrases.english: If he needs his house built, his fence put up,
or his field reaped —
the friend goes to workers whom he regularly hires,
and says to them:
"So-and-so is forbidden by a vow to benefit from me
and I don't know what I can do for him."
They do the work for him,
and they come and take their wages from this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a parallel case about workers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Labor, like food, may be arranged indirectly through familiar workers, who collect their wages from the friend.

steps.title: On the road: give the food to a third person as a gift
steps.stepSummary: If the two are traveling and the forbidden man has no food, the friend may give food to a third person as a gift, and the forbidden man may take it from him and eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were walking on the road and he had nothing to eat, the friend gives food to someone else as a gift. That person takes it and eats it, and this is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another case in the same spirit as the storekeeper and the workers. Here the two men are traveling together, and the one who may not benefit from his friend has no food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friend may not give the food straight to the forbidden man, because that would be direct benefit. Instead he gives it as a real gift to a third person. The food now belongs to that person, so when the forbidden man gets it from him, it does not come from the friend.

phrases.english: If they were walking along the road,
and he does not have with him anything to eat,
phrases.notes: "He" is the man who is not allowed to benefit from his friend.

phrases.english: the friend gives food to another person as a gift,
and that one takes and eats, and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a third case (travel), after the storekeeper and workers cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While traveling, the friend may give food as a gift to a third person, and the forbidden man may take it from him and eat.

steps.title: No third person: declare the food ownerless
steps.stepSummary: If no one else is there, the friend puts the food on a rock or fence and declares it ownerless for anyone. The forbidden man may take it and eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is nobody else there, he puts the food on a rock or a fence and says: 'This is ownerless for anyone who wants it.' The other man takes it and eats, and this is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה handles the harder version of the road case, when there is no third person to receive the gift. The solution is to make the food הפקר, ownerless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once food is הפקר, it belongs to nobody. Whoever picks it up gets it from no one, not from the friend. So the forbidden man is taking ownerless food, not getting benefit from his friend.

phrases.english: And if there is no other person there,
he places the food on a rock
or on a fence,
and says: "They are hereby ownerless
for anyone who wants them,"
and that one takes and eats, and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fallback for the road case when no third person is available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no one else is present, the friend may declare the food הפקר, and the forbidden man may take it and eat.

steps.title: רבי יוסי forbids the ownerless method
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and forbids this method.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by saying that רבי יוסי disagrees with the ruling just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allowed the forbidden man to take food that his friend declared הפקר. רבי יוסי does not accept this solution. The משנה does not give his reason, so the גמרא will explain it next.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei forbids it.
phrases.notes: He is arguing about the ownerless-food case just mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion about the הפקר case in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי forbids using הפקר in this case.

steps.title: רבא begins to explain רבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why רבי יוסי forbids it and starts to answer: it is a rabbinic safeguard (גזירה) because of another case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רבי יוסי's reason? It is a decree because of...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets out to explain why רבי יוסי forbids the הפקר method. His answer starts here and finishes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not say that הפקר fails to work on its own terms. He says רבי יוסי's ruling is a גזירה, a safeguard the רבנן added to prevent a mistake in a different case. The case it is guarding against is named in the next words.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. רבא's full reason, meaning which case the גזירה is guarding against, comes right after this.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
It is a decree because of...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יוסי's disagreement in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's ruling is a rabbinic גזירה, not a rule that הפקר fails to work. The case it guards against is named in the continuation.
